dataset_title: Farm-scale grass bunker-silo loss and management summary extract
source_title: Dry matter losses of grass, lucerne and maize silages in bunker silos
source_location: Table 2 p. 147; Table 3 and Results p. 148; Methods pp. 145–146
material_scope: 26 grass silos on one organic and two conventional Bavarian farms; data collected 2008–2011; sealed for at least 6 weeks; feed-out averaged 3 months; grass sources included permanent grassland and some grass-clover/annual ryegrass.
data_type: primary farm measurements reported as summary statistics; underlying silo-level rows not reported as an open data file
license_or_rights: Publisher/article page identifies copyright; no explicit open reuse license was confirmed. Only a short factual summary with attribution is stored; do not redistribute the article PDF.
measurement_scope: Total-in vs total-out dry-matter accounting over silo ensiling/storage and feed-out. Not storage-only and not a temporal kinetic curve.
negative_loss_handling: The source explicitly attributes negative loss estimates to measurement/accounting error. Preserve the reported minimum for audit only; never use it as a physical negative loss or model coefficient.
limitations: German dairy-farm bunker silage, not roadside/VARTA biomass or GreenHub storage. Total-in versus total-out covers silo ensiling/storage and feed-out as a combined interval; it is not a duration-resolved degradation kinetic or an aerobic-versus-anaerobic comparison. Negative reported loss is measurement/accounting error, not physical mass gain and must not be used as a negative loss coefficient. No runtime mapping or default.
No raw observations per silo or time series are deposited in the article; summary sample counts vary by metric.
citation: Köhler et al. (2013). Dry matter losses of grass, lucerne and maize silages in bunker silos. Agricultural and Food Science 22:145–150. https://doi.org/10.23986/afsci.6715
